parts.problem_md: For a named settlement in a LEDC country, describe the social challenges brought about by urban growth.
parts.solution_md:
Urban growth in Mumbai has led to the creation of India's largest slum, Dharavi **[KU],** with over 700,000 inhabitants. Up to 1000 new migrants arrive in Mumbai each day, and the lack of housing in the city means that many must build their own houses on land that does not belong to them.  There is a constant threat of eviction for people who live in informal settlements. **[KU]**

Sanitation in Dharavi is poor, with many residents relying on shared toilets and water taps.  Up to 100 people can share a toilet.** ****[KU]**** ** This means that diseases such as cholera and typhoid can spread quickly, reducing life expectancy.** ****[KU]**

There is a lack of healthcare, with many relying on the services provided by NGOs such as Project Mumbai. **[KU]** There are often long waiting times for health treatment.  Urban growth also leads to air pollution, and this can impact the health of inhabitants, leading to respiratory diseases and cancers. **[KU]**

Literacy rates in Dharavi are 69% (20% lower than the Mumbai average)  because children are often needed to help earn money for their families rather than attend school. **[KU]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> The command word is 'describe', which means that the answer needs to state in detail what the issues are, using a detailed, specific example.
> 
> **Mark allocation**
> 
> This is a 'level of response' answer. Each point made in the answer does not equal a mark.
> 
> AO focus = AO1 **[KU]**
> 
> - A top-level 3 **[7 marks]** answer will include specific examples that show:
> 
>   - Knowledge of the challenges caused by urban growth
>   - Understanding of the impacts that urban growth has on a settlement
> 
> **Alternative content**
> 
> The answer above is just one example of a response to this question. Other locations, such as informal housing in Rio or Lagos, are equally valid

> **[exam-tip]**
> Make sure the answer is related to social challenges and does not focus on environmental or economic problems.
> 
> You would be credited for the discussion of air pollution if you linked it to the health of people,  but not if you mentioned it as an environmental issue.

parts.problem_md: Explain the environmental impacts of urban sprawl on the rural–urban fringe.
parts.solution_md:
Deforestation needs to take place to clear space for housebuilding **[1],** and this leads to the loss of biodiversity as trees are cut down **[1]**.  It also means there is less photosynthesis, so the amount of CO₂ in the atmosphere remains the same **[1]**, which can lead to increased climate change. Pollution increases as a result of increased traffic congestion. **[1]**  Many people living in the rural urban fringe will rely on cars to access other parts of the settlement. **[1]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> The command word is 'explain', which means that the answer needs to provide an outline of how deforestation can impact the natural environment.
> 
> **Mark allocation**
> 
> - **One mark** for each simple point
> - **One mark** for each development of the simple point
> 
> **[5 marks]**
> 
> Answers can be either:
> 
> - Five simple points
> - One developed point plus three simple points
> - Two points which are developed plus one simple point
> 
> **Alternate content**
> 
> The answer above is just one example of a response to this question. Other information that could be used in the answer includes:
> 
> - Flooding – as more impermeable surfaces are created, there is more surface runoff and less infiltration

parts.problem_md: For a named urban area you have studied, describe what has been done to improve quality of life in a squatter settlement
parts.solution_md:
| **Indicative content** | **General guidance** | |---|---| | Key features of improvement schemes focus on

- Sanitation
- Education
- Health
- Building quality
- Reducing pollution
- Crime

Popular examples include

- Rochina in Rio
- Dharavi in Mumbai
- Kibera in Lagos

But any other squatter settlement is accepted | The command word ‘describe’ requires you to say what the main features of the improvement were

7 mark questions are level marked rather than point marked.

You should refer to specific locations and examples, you need to do more than name a city and squatter settlement

If you do not name an example you can only score 5 marks maximum

The top level is achieved by including comprehensive and accurate statements including place specific reference | | **Model Answer** | **Commentary** | |---|---| | Rocinha is the largest squatter settlement in Rio with a population of 75,000. Problems in Rocinha included high crime, poorly constructed buildings, a lack of clean water and diseases.

Top-down schemes are operated by the government. The government has spent over £200 million to set up self-help schemes in the area. People get tools, training and loans. The local authority provides materials and the locals do the work. This has improved the quality of life because the houses are safer and locals learn a skill that can help them get a job. It also saves money which could be used to pay for other improvements. Electricity and sewage systems have been installed.

The Brazilian bank has also offered people in the squatter settlements 100% mortgages to buy a house and this should mean that they continue to improve the area.

A local police force, The Pacifying Police Unit, has also been set up to reduce the crime rate in squatter settlements.

Bottom-up schemes are led by charities or locals and are usually less expensive. The Favela Foundation has been set up to offer free classes to people living in the squatter settlements. They donate books, pens and desks as well as funding school trips for children. This means that people will have a better chance of getting a formal job when they are older. In Rocinha there is now a university.

There are only two health clinics in Rocinha and disease rates are much higher in the squatter settlement than elsewhere. Health kits were delivered to homes and this has improved life this has improved life expectancy by helping to detect and treat diseases. | **Marks awarded 7/7**

This is one possible way to answer this question – your answer does not have to be exactly the same

There should be a range of schemes to include top-down and bottom-up.

This answer scores level 7 because it includes:

- Detailed statements
- Place specific examples |

parts.problem_md:
For a named urban area, describe the causes of a problem faced by the residents and explain how the authorities in that urban area are attempting to solve it.

Name of urban area .....................
parts.solution_md:
Levels marking
Note: one problem only, if more than one then credit the best answer.
Level 1 (1–3 marks)
Statements including limited detail which describe the causes of an urban problem and/or explain how authorities are attempting to solve it.
Note: no credit at L1 for listing problems.
Level 2 (4–6 marks)
More developed statements which describe the causes of an urban problem and/or explain how authorities are attempting to solve it.
Use of valid statistics (max. 1 × L2);
Note: simple cause and solution = 2 × L1 and not 1 × L2;
Max. 5 if no named or inappropriate example.
Level 3 (7 marks)
Uses named example.
Comprehensive and accurate statements which describe the causes of an urban problem and explain how authorities are attempting to solve it, with some place specific reference.
Content Guide:
Content will depend on the problem selected and these are likely to relate to urban problems such as:
Traffic issues,
Inequality,
Housing issues,
Conflicts over land use change,
Specified pollution,
Crime,
Poverty,
Unemployment.
These are the problems listed in the syllabus, but the list is not exhaustive, and all examples used should be credited if appropriate causes and solutions are referred to.
Place specific reference is likely to consist of:
Locational details,
Specific details of the urban area chosen, etc.

parts.problem_md: For an urban area you have studied, describe the impact of urbanisation on people who live there.
parts.solution_md:
| **Indicative content** | **General guidance** | |---|---| | - Economic
- Social
- Environmental | The command word ‘describe’ requires you to give some information about the changes that have occurred

7 mark questions are level marked rather than point marked.

You should refer to specific locations and examples, you need to do more than name a town

If you do not name an example you can only score 5 marks maximum

The top level is achieved by including comprehensive and accurate statements including some place specific reference | | **Model Answer** | **Commentary** | |---|---| | Rural to urban migration has caused Mumbai’s population to grow rapidly and it has 20 million people living there.

Rapid urbanisation has led to high levels of unemployment in Mumbai, at 8%. Many people are forced to work in the informal sector where there is no job security and poor conditions which impacts quality of life.

The transport system cannot cope with the large numbers of people and so congestion is a real problem. It can take hours to make a short journey in the city and the large number of cars creates air pollution. People are suffering with breathing problems. The air quality is six times more than the recommended limit and air pollution has caused 14,000 deaths in Mumbai since 2021.

Crime rates in Mumbai are high and have increased by 10% since 2021. Bribery is the most common crime.

There is a shortage of housing in the city and so many people live in squatter settlements such as Dharavi. The conditions are poor, with overcrowding and a lack of sanitation. There is one toilet for every 1440 people.

The hospitals and schools in Mumbai are overcrowded. There is a shortage of doctors and teachers and so people have to wait a long time for treatment | **Marks awarded 7/7**

This is one possible way to answer this question – your answer does not have to be exactly the same

There must be specific reference to the strategies used. Try to describe a range of impacts

This answer scores level 7 because it includes:

- Detailed statements
- Place specific examples |
